dhp44:1: Who shall overcome this earth, and this World of Yama, and the World of the Gods?
dhp44:3: Who shall pluck the well-taught Words of Truth, even as a good man plucks a flower?
dhp45:1: The disciple shall overcome this earth, and this World of Yama, and the World of the Gods.
dhp45:3: The disciple shall pluck the well-taught Words of Truth, even as a good man plucks a flower.
dhp46:1: He who knows that this body is like foam, he who clearly comprehends that it is of the nature of a mirage,
dhp46:3: Such a man will break the flower-tipped arrows of Māra and will go where the King of Death will not see him.
dhp47:1: Even while a man is gathering flowers and is absorbed in pleasure,
dhp47:3: Death comes and carries him off, even as a mighty flood overwhelms a sleeping village.
dhp48:1: Even while a man is gathering flowers, while his heart is absorbed in pleasure,
dhp48:3: Even before he has satisfied his desires, death overpowers him.
dhp49:1: Even as a bee, without injuring a flower, or the color, or the scent thereof,
dhp49:3: Gathers the honey, and then flies away, even so should a sage go about village.
dhp50:1: Not the faults of others, not things done and left undone by others,
dhp50:3: Only one’s own sins of commission and omission should one regard.
dhp51:1: Like a beautiful flower that possesses color but lacks perfume,
dhp51:3: So well-spoken words are fruitless to him that doeth them not.
dhp52:1: Like a beautiful flower that possesses both color and perfume,
dhp52:3: So well-spoken words are fruitful to him that doeth them.
dhp53:1: Even as from a heap of flowers a man may make many garlands,
dhp53:3: Even so he that is born a mortal man should perform many good deeds.
dhp54:1: The perfume of flowers goes not against the wind,
dhp54:2: Nor that of sandal, nor that of Tagara or Mallikā flowers;
dhp54:3: But the perfume of the righteous goes against the wind;
dhp55:1: To every point a good man exhales fragrance,
dhp55:2: Whether of sandal or of lotus
dhp55:3: Or of Tagara or Vassikī flowers,
dhp55:4: The perfume of virtue is preeminent.
dhp56:1: Weak is this perfume, this perfume of Tagara and of sandal;
dhp56:3: The perfume of the virtuous is the finest that is wafted to the gods.
dhp57:1: If men are endowed with the virtues, live the life of Heedfulness,
dhp57:3: Are emancipated through perfect knowledge, Māra can never find the way to them.
dhp58:1: As upon a heap of rubbish cast out on the highway,
dhp58:3: The lotus will grow, sweetly fragrant, delighting the heart,
dhp59:1: Even so, among them that are as rubbish, blind folk, unconverted,
dhp59:3: The disciple of the Supremely Enlightened shines with exceeding glory because of wisdom.
